title: Comparison of MEMS PZT Cantilevers Based on $d_{31}$  and $d_{33}$ Modes for Vibration Energy Harvesting

sections.heading: Comparison of MEMS PZT Cantilevers Based on d31 and $d _ { 3 3 }$ Modes for Vibration Energy Harvesting
sections.text:
Seon-Bae Kim, Hyejin Park, Seung-Hyun Kim, H. Clyde Wikle, III, Jung-Hyun Park, and Dong-Joo Kim

Abstract— $\mathbf { \mathcal { d } _ { 3 1 } }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode microelectromechanical systems piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) were fabricated and compared to investigate their output powers converted from vibration. Both types of devices have the same dimensions in a cantilever structure and aim to effectively couple vibration from ambient conditions. The resonant frequencies of the cantilevers are $2 4 3 \mathbf { H z }$ Two types of devices were compared using mathematical equations based on an equivalent circuit model. The output power of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH was $2 . 1 5 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ and $2 . 3 3 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ in experiment and modeling, respectively. The $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEHs generated output power ranging between 0.62 and $1 . 7 1 \ \mu \mathrm { W }$ when the width of the interdigital electrode (IDE) is ranging from 8 to $1 6 \mu \mathrm { m }$ and finger spacing is varied from 4 to $1 6 \ \mu \mathrm { m }$ . The output power of the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device strongly depends on the dimensions of IDE. The analysis of material constant and electrode design was conducted in conjunction with developing a mathematical equation. The result predicts that the output power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH can be higher than that of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH when the finger width is reduced to $2 \mu \mathbf { m }$ and finger spacing is between 8 and $2 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m }$ . [2012-0068]

Index Terms—Energy harvesting, lead zirconate titanate (PZT), piezoelectric cantilevers, piezoelectric mode, piezoelectric transducers, vibration energy harvesters.

#

T HE piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) is one of themost promising devices to generate electric energy from renewable energy sources. In particular, PEH is of interest in wireless and mobile devices as an alternative energy supply since the feature size of the devices becomes smaller and power consumption increases with diversified functions. PEHs can offer the ability to meet application requirements such as compatibility for miniaturization and high efficiency in energy conversion. The energy source for PEH is mechanical energy, mostly vibration, which induces strain in the piezoelectric layer, and thus polarization according to poling direction. Three piezoelectric modes can be considered for PEH, i.e., $d _ { 3 1 }$ $d _ { 3 3 }$ , and $d _ { 1 5 }$ modes according to the stress and polarization direction. The realization of PEH using different piezoelectric modes is dependent on electrode configuration. A $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode

PEH possesses top and bottom electrodes (TBEs), and its fabrication is relatively simple. In addition, the microstructure of piezoelectric layers can be modified by the type and structure of the bottom electrode, which results in the performance of PEH. Many studies have been reported to improve the power density of a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH. The performance has been improved by several approaches such as a modification of cantilever shape to a trapezoidal design [1], nonlinear vibration using magnetic force [2], [3], use of epitaxial piezoelectric materials [4], [5], and novel structure with air-spaced cantilever [6], [7]. A $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH is fabricated with the interdigital electrode (IDE) introduced by Hagood et al. [8] and Wilkie et al. [9]. Reports on $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEHs are relatively less compared to those on $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEHs owing to the complexity of IDE fabrication. Fabrication of IDEs requires fine patterning while PEH with TBE needs simple rectangular shape patterning. When the piezoelectric material in a PEH is poled, higher voltage is required for a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device since the finger spacing of IDE is generally wider than the distance between electrodes in TBE. Such high voltage can cause device failure resulting from electric breakdown. IDE configuration also influences the output power of a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH, but its power is typically lower than that of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEHs [10], [11]. A $d _ { 1 5 }$ mode PEH can be considered because of higher piezoelectric constant, but the fabrication of the device is not straightforward because electrodes for poling and charge collection should be different. Therefore, $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode-based PEHs offer a convenient fabrication process for applications.

For the design of a structure to convert mechanical vibration to electricity, the cantilever is one of the basic structures since displacement can be easily generated in a transverse direction upon vibration. Electric charge is induced perpendicular or parallel to the direction of applied stress in either $d _ { 3 1 }$ or $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices, respectively, as illustrated in Fig. 1. The open circuit voltage $V _ { \mathrm { o c } }$ is proportional to stress $\sigma _ { \mathrm { i j } }$ , voltage constant $g _ { \mathrm { i j } }$ , and the distance between electrodes $G _ { e }$ , as given in (1) [12]. The voltage constant equation is shown in (2), where $d _ { \mathrm { i j } }$ is the piezoelectric constant and the subscript denotes the direction of stress and polarization; $\varepsilon _ { r }$ is the relative dielectric constant, and $\varepsilon _ { \mathrm { 0 } }$ is the permittivity of vacuum [13]. Lead zirconate titanate (PZT), one of the most popular piezoelectric materials, exhibits approximately two times higher piezoelectric constant in $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode than in $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode, so the voltage constant is expected to be double for a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device compared to a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device when both modes have the same dielectric constants. Generated voltage in PEH is proportional to the distance between electrodes, i.e., distance between the top and the bottom electrode in a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH and distance between the electrode fingers in a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH. The film thickness of PZT for microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) is relatively thin, which commonly results in shorter distance between electrodes in $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH than in $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device. Therefore, the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH has the advantage in obtaining higher voltage while the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode can be superior in large current generation. In the case of output power determined by the product of voltage and current, better performance was reported from $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH than the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device due to low capacitance in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device [14]. In contrast, the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device exhibited better performance than the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device in actuator applications [15]

In addition to generated voltage and current, other factors such as the degree of poling and the easiness of microfabrication should be considered. Poling piezoelectric layer underneath finger electrodes in $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode can be hard due to dead layer effect [16], [17]. Electrodes in a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH are located on the same side of piezoelectric layer while electrodes in a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device are stacked sequentially on different layers. Hence, one more etching or deposition mask is required for the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device fabrication than that for the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device. Clearly, the performance and merits of a PEH can be strongly dependent on the type of piezoelectric mode. However, the characteristics of $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEHs were not studied systematically.

In this paper, two piezoelectric mode-based PEHs were fabricated with the same dimensions of piezoelectric layers. The output powers of both PEHs were characterized and compared with analytical equations.

sections.heading: II. DEVICE FABRICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION
sections.text:
Both types of PEHs were fabricated from 4-in silicon-oninsulator (SOI) wafers to accurately define the thickness of cantilevers. The SOI wafers were composed of a $5 0 0 \mathrm { - n m }$ -thick $\mathrm { S i O _ { 2 } }$ layer for electrical passivation, a $2 0 \mathrm { - } \mu \mathrm { m } \cdot$ -thick Si device layer, a $5 0 0 \mathrm { - n m }$ -thick buried $\mathrm { S i O _ { 2 } }$ layer, and a $5 0 0 \mathrm { - } \mu \mathrm { m } \cdot$ -thick Si handle layer. The $\mathrm { P t / T i }$ layer was coated on a SOI wafer as a bottom electrode prior to the deposition of PZT film in a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device. $\mathrm { Z r O _ { 2 } }$ and $\mathrm { P b T i O _ { 3 } }$ were deposited as a seed layer for the PZT film in a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device. $\mathrm { P b ( Z r _ { 0 . 5 2 } T i _ { 0 . 4 8 } ) O _ { 3 } }$ solution was synthesized by Inostek Inc., and $1 \not { p } | | \mathrm { { m } }$ -thick PZT was deposited by spin coating followed by a heat treatment. Both $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices use $\mathrm { P t }$ for the electrode on PZT. Twelve sets of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices were fabricated with a combination of finger widths $w _ { f }$ (8, 12, and $1 6 ~ \mu \mathrm { m } )$ and spacing $s _ { f }$ (4, 8, 12, and $1 6 \mu \mathrm { m } ,$ ). A top view of the IDE pattern is schematically illustrated in Fig. 2. The cantilever and proof mass were defined by reactive ion etching. The dimensions of the cantilever were $1 0 0 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } \times 3 0 0 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } \times 2 1 \ \mu \mathrm { m }$ , and the dimensions of the proof mass were $1 0 0 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } \times 2 0 0 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } \times$ $5 0 0 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ (width  length $\times$ thickness). Four photomasks were used to fabricate the $d _ { 3 1 }$ devices, while only three photomasks were used to fabricate the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices. Further details of the fabrication process can be found in our previous work [18]. The images of the final devices are shown in Fig. 3.

All the fabricated devices were poled at $1 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ with applying a field of $2 0 0  { \mathrm { ~ k V / c m } }$ for $1 0 \ \mathrm { m i n }$ . The capacitance and impedance were characterized with an HP 4192A LF impedance analyzer. The structure of PZT films was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Bruker D-8). Polarization versus electric field was measured with a ferroelectric analyzer (aixACCT, TF analyzer) and a Radiant Ferroelectric System (Precision LC, P-HVI). The output power was measured under $0 . 5 – \mathrm { g }$ $\mathrm { ~  ~ \mathcal ~ { ~ 1 ~ g ~ } ~ } = 9 . 8 \mathrm { ~ \ m / s ^ { 2 } ~ }$ ) vibration. The maximum power was measured with a resistive load at the resonant frequency. Details of the measurement setup can be found elsewhere [19].

sections.heading: IV. RESULT AND DISCUSSION
sections.text:
Fig. 4 depicts the XRD patterns of the PZT films used to fabricate $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices. The PZT films were grown in different orientations due to different underneath layers where PZT layers were coated from chemical solution. Piezoelectric anisotropy, however, would not be significant since the degree of orientation is not considerable by exhibiting mixed orientation. In addition, the in-plane crystallographic orientation of PZT films will be more random due to their polycrystalline structure. Fig. 5(a) shows the polarization-versus-electric field $( P { - } E )$ curve of a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device. Fig. 5(b) also presents the $P { - } E$ curves for a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device in which the finger width and spacing are 8 and $4 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ , respectively. For both devices, it is apparent that the dipole alignment can be saturated at $2 0 0 \ \mathrm { k V / c m }$ . The PZT film in a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device shows higher polarization compared to that in a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device. Such difference can be attributed to the following reasons. The curves in Fig. 5(a) and (b) were slanted. This phenomenon is frequently observed in other studies [10], [11], [34], [35], and the slant angle and polarization values were found to increase as finger spacing increases in a PZT with IDE [34], [35]. A large amount of charge injection in a small electrode area could be responsible for the higher polarization value in PZT films of a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device than that of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH. The total electrode area patterned in PZT films is smaller in IDE than in TBE, as given in Table II. Han et al. measured $P { - } E$ curves of thick PZT films at various electrode sizes, and they observed higher polarization in PZT films with a smaller top electrode. A larger amount of charge injection in a smaller electrode was suggested [36]. ![](images/25c915fe8f85a5a6c555e13affcea5e006fded90f59cbdfe7e20ba404214baca.jpg) Fig. 5. $P { - } E$ hysteresis curves from (a) $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH and (b) $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH—finger width and spacing are 8 and $4 \mu \mathrm m$ , respectively. Fig. 6 shows the voltage and output power measured from two types of devices with varying resistive load. The power generated by a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH was measured to be $2 . 1 5 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ and calculated as $2 . 3 3 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ under $0 . 5 – \mathrm { g }$ vibration. The output power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEHs ranged from 0.62 to $1 . 7 1 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ i n measurement and from 0.78 to $2 . 1 8 ~ \mu \mathrm { W }$ from the analytical equation. The capacitance of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device was $3 3 . 2 \mu \mathrm { F }$ , and that of the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device ranged between 170 and $6 9 2 \mathrm { p F }$ . The optimum resistance values to obtain maximum power were $9 . 8 8 \mathrm { k } \Omega$ for $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $8 0 \mathrm { k } \Omega$ to $1 \ : \mathbf { M } \Omega$ for $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices. The lower capacitance and higher matching impedance in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device than in the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device shows agreement with Sodano’s report [14]. The differences in matching impedance and capacitance were explained by matching impedance inverse proportional to capacitance and small capacitance by using IDE in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device, respectively. Since the output power of a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device is strongly dependent on electrode dimensions, the output power of the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEHs was obtained at various finger widths and finger spacing as shown in Fig. 7. Solid lines represent measured values, and dashed lines show calculated values. The measured power of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices shows approximately $92 \%$ in comparison with the estimated power, while the power from $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices exhibits $7 5 \% - 8 0 \%$ of the calculated power. This difference between measured and calculated values might originate from the range of values reported for the piezoelectric constant in the literature. A lot of references are available to present piezoelectric constant $d _ { 3 1 }$ in PZT films prepared by various deposition methods, but the piezoelectric constant $d _ { 3 3 }$ of PZT films is rarely reported. Part of the reason may lie in the difficult measurement since the $d _ { 3 1 }$ constant is measured in the out-of-plane direction while out $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices are poled in the in-plane direction [30]. Modeling, however, appears to be consistent with measurement when considering the tendency of output power change and value in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices. It is, therefore, reasonable to estimate the output power of PEHs using the two output power models. ![](images/4ce6496d48e89d023f804fca66d0cf0a875572302da4cb79390e54de60b9f13e.jpg) Fig. 7. Estimated power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH with various values of finger width as a function of finger spacing. The dotted line denotes the power of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device $( 2 . 1 5 \mu \mathrm { W } )$ with identical cantilever dimension. The output power of $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices shows higher values than that of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices in our fabricated devices, but $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices could produce much higher power if the dead space in a piezoelectric layer is reduced by decreasing the finger width or the PZT layer contributing to power generation is maximized by approaching finger spacing towards effective finger spacing. As shown in Fig. 8, the output power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices was estimated with an IDE configuration extended beyond those devices for which measurements were made to find a configuration exhibiting higher output power than a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device with identical overall dimensions. Assuming that a real device can generate $7 5 \%$ of the calculated output power, i.e., observed maximum deviation between calculated and measured output, the output power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH could exceed that of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device when the finger width is reduced to $2 \ \mu \mathrm { m }$ , and finger spacing is between 8 and $2 0 \ \mu \mathrm { { m } }$ , ignoring difficulty in dc poling. ![](images/3d44345129b7722e77ce004ee1d794ea3f9aa2906b454e797fcd4295c891aa4e.jpg) Fig. 9. Open circuit voltage variation as a function of electrode spacing in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices with various finger widths. The dashed line represents the open circuit voltage of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device multiplied by finger spacing, i.e., spacing between the top and the bottom electrode is $1 ~ \mu \mathrm { m }$ in the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device, and the open circuit voltage of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device was multiplied by 4–16 (electrode spacing of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices) in order to compare open circuit voltage at identical electrode spacing with $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices. There are three factors contributing to the difference between the $d _ { 3 1 }$ and the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device in power generation: the piezoelectric voltage constant, spacing between electrodes, and electrode area. It is necessary to determine the dominant role between the piezoelectric material and electrode design on the performance of a PEH. Piezoelectric voltage constants can be calculated by using (2), resulting in 0.00497 for $g _ { 3 1 }$ and 0.00452 for $g _ { 3 3 }$ . A higher piezoelectric voltage constant may be anticipated from the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device when considering only piezoelectric constant $( d )$ without the influence of the dielectric constant in $d _ { 3 3 }$ and $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices. In our experimental result, the dielectric constant of the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device was found to exceed approximately two times that of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device. Therefore, higher output voltage observed in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device is attributed to electrode design, i.e., spacing between electrodes, than material constants $( g )$ . Fig. 9 shows the increase of output voltage (open circuit voltage) with electrode spacing. When plotting calculated output voltages from the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device with varying the spacing between the top and the bottom electrode, i.e., film thickness, similar output voltage can be obtained, indicating the important role of electrode design in $d _ { 3 3 }$ and $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices. Table II compares the geometrical factors of $d _ { 3 3 }$ and $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices such as the electrode area, spacing between electrodes, and volume of piezoelectric layer contributing to power generation. The $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device used for this comparison has finger width and spacing of 2 and $1 2 \ \mu \mathrm { { m } }$ , respectively. The large electrode area is preferred in the electrode design of the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device, and the wide electrode spacing is for the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device. For identical overall dimensions of the cantilever structure, the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH can generate higher output power than the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH, although the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode PEH has larger volume of piezoelectric layer contributing to power generation than the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH. The output power of $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices can be predicted by two electrode parameters, i.e., electrode area responsible for current generation and electrode spacing for voltage generation, because the output power is calculated by the product of current and voltage. In a typical application, a PEH is equipped with a circuit for rectification and a rechargeable battery or a capacitor for storage [37]. The rectification circuit is made of diodes with a minimum threshold voltage to allow forward conduction. With higher generated voltage from a PEH, there would be less limitation in rectification circuit design and less loss during rectification for practical applications. Therefore, in view of device application, a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device can be superior to a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device because higher voltage and power can be obtained mainly by electrode design. In contrast, $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode devices can be beneficial compared with $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices from a production standpoint because of a simpler photomask design that does not require fine patterning necessary for IDEs.

sections.heading: V. CONCLUSION
sections.text: Two piezoelectric, $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ , mode PEHs were fabricated and characterized to compare the converted output power from environment vibration. The output power of the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device was varied by IDE configuration, and output power modeling was performed to estimate the power generation of the devices with finger widths and spacing beyond those fabricated. The optimal IDE design predicted from the calculation presents higher output power in the $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode device than in the $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device. The piezoelectric voltage constant of piezoelectric films in $d _ { 3 1 }$ and $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode devices appears a minor factor for the output power of PZT-based PEHs in terms of piezoelectric mode. The factors related to electrode design such as electrode spacing and electrode area play more a important role in the power generation capabilities of PEHs. Ignoring practical issues with fabrication, a $d _ { 3 3 }$ mode PEH can be favorable over a $d _ { 3 1 }$ mode device for application because higher voltage and power can be obtained with appropriate IDE design.
